common:
**From:** Priya Nandakumar  
**To:** Cody  
**Subject:** RE: Halberd & Vale, MSEDGEWIN10

Morning, Cody.

I forwarded your report to Tomás at 06:40. He called me at 06:52, which tells you how it landed.

After reading it, Tomás went and sat with the receptionist. The "supplier invoice" came in an email from a domain one letter off from their real stationery supplier. It had a ZIP attached, and inside the ZIP was `Invoice@0582.cpl`. She dragged it into Downloads, double-clicked it, saw nothing happen, and went back to paying bills. The PC has been pulled for reimaging, the email has been purged from every mailbox at Halberd & Vale, and their mail filter now strips `.cpl` files, zipped or not.

Notice what happened there: the logs couldn't tell us how that file arrived, and you were right not to guess. The answer came from a person sitting down at a desk, *because* your report told them exactly what to ask.

"I think the agent just doesn't like our accounting stuff." Remember that sentence. You'll hear versions of it every week.

by_grade.S: Honestly? That's the cleanest first report I've had from a new hire. Every claim had a record number, you knew the difference between Windows plumbing and the attacker's code, and your unknowns list is better than some of my seniors'. I've put it in the team wiki as the example. Don't let it go to your head.
by_grade.A: Strong work. Your core findings were right and properly evidenced. A couple of the subtler details got past you. Read the reference write-up and see which ones. That's the difference between good and great in this job, and it's learnable.
by_grade.B: Solid start. You found the important part, but you left points on the table. The quieter details in that export, a path that doesn't match and a record that isn't there, matter more than they look. Go through the reference investigation slowly, line by line, against your own notes. Dee says the second case is where it clicks for most people.
by_grade.C: You got the shape of it, but too much of the report rests on things you didn't prove. That's normal on night one. Dee will sit with you tomorrow and walk through the export field by field. Then rerun the case cold. Seriously: reset it and do it again.
by_grade.D: Rough first night, and that's fine. Everyone has one. Before the next shift, reset this case and work it again from the top with the toolkit notes open. Read every field of every event. Don't open a single hint until you've written down what you think it means.

next:
---

**One more thing.** Dee caught me on my way out:

> "That `rundll32` → script-host chain you flagged? I ran a hunt for script engines with `rundll32.exe` as their parent across the other clients. Got a hit at **Corvid Logistics** from last week. Different trick, rundll32 running something that isn't a DLL at all, and on that machine *something stayed behind after reboot*. Want to give the new hire a crack at it?"

I told her I'd ask you. Get some sleep first.

— Priya

**Chapter 2: Echoes in the Scheduler** is coming.
